Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to keep my name off the recording for now, but I'm happy to answer your questions.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Conroe, Texas, on the main road heading toward the shopping center. I was changing lanes to get into the
right lane because my turn was coming up.
Q: What were the weather and road conditions like?
A: It was clear and dry. Traffic was moderate, nothing unusual for that stretch.
Q: Walk me through what happened as you moved over.
A: I checked my mirror, saw the lane looked open, and signaled. I started to move over slowly. Then I felt a bump on
my side and heard scraping. The other car had come up alongside me in the lane I was entering.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began your lane change?
A: Not directly. I looked in the mirror and didn't see anything close, but I may not have checked my blind spot as
thoroughly as I should have.
Q: Did you stop or pull over after the contact?
A: Yes, I pulled onto the shoulder a short distance away. Both cars were still drivable, so we moved them out of the
traffic flow.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My neck and lower back started hurting within an hour or so. It's a stiff, aching pain, and turning my head is
uncomfortable.
Q: Have you sought medical care?
A: I went to a clinic the same day and was told I had strains in my neck and back. I've been doing home exercises
and taking over-the-counter pain relievers.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and get my car repaired. Thank you for your time.
Q: Thank you. This cocnludes the statement.
</page>
